questions.question: 35112. Transaction___________________
questions.option1: can be a little tricky when it comes to corporate accounting.
questions.option2: Accrual accounting recognizes it immediately after it is finalized, regardless of when payment is received or made.
questions.option3: Cash accounting is used mostly by smaller businesses and records it only when money is received or paid out.
questions.explain:
Transactions can be a little tricky when it comes to corporate accounting.
Accrual accounting recognizes a transaction immediately after it is finalized, regardless of when payment is received or made.
Cash accounting is used mostly by smaller businesses and records a transaction only when money is received or paid out.
Third-party transactions can often complicate the process.

questions.question: 35111. Which is the federal agency that oversees investment offerings and financial markets in Bangladesh?
questions.explain:
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is the U.S. government oversight agency responsible for regulating the securities markets and protecting investors.
The Securities Exchange Act of 1934 established the SEC, mainly in response to the stock market crash of 1929 in the leadup to the Great Depression.
The SEC is responsible for regulating financial markets and approving securities for sale to the public.
The SEC brings civil action against those it alleges broke securities laws or regulations.

questions.question: 35110. Which is incorrect for Profit?
questions.option1: Profit refers to the money companies keep after paying all of their expenses.
questions.option2: Operating profit accounts for expenses like overhead and depreciation.
questions.option3: Net profit equals sales minus the cost of goods sold.
questions.option4: Companies can distribute profits to shareholders as dividends or reinvest them back into the business.
questions.explain:
Profit refers to the money companies keep after paying all of their expenses.
Gross profit equals sales minus the cost of goods sold.
Operating profit accounts for expenses like overhead and depreciation.
Net profit is also referred to as the bottom line.
Companies can distribute profits to shareholders as dividends or reinvest them back into the business.

questions.question: 35109. Which is not an advantages of partnership business?
questions.option1: Combine labor and capital to launch
questions.option4: Variety of experiences and new perspectives
questions.explain: Partnerships offer several advantages, including shared financial burdens, diverse skill sets, and simplified operations. They can also foster greater access to capital and credit, and potentially lower individual tax burdens. Additionally, partnerships can be easier to establish than some other business structures.

questions.question: 35108. _____________ is calculated as revenue minus expenses, interest, and taxes.
questions.explain:
Net income (NI) is calculated as revenue minus expenses, interest, and taxes.
Earnings per share (EPS) are calculated using NI.
Investors should review the numbers used to calculate NI because expenses can be hidden in accounting methods, or revenues can be inflated.
NI also represents an individual’s total earnings or pretax earnings after factoring deductions and taxes in gross income.

questions.question: 35107. Market share________________
questions.option1: the percentage of an industry's total sales over a certain period that a particular company can claim.
questions.option2: calculated by dividing total company sales by total industry sales.
questions.option3: provides a general idea of the size of a company in relation to its market and competitors.
questions.explain:
Market share is the percentage of an industry's total sales over a certain period that a particular company can claim.
It is calculated by dividing total company sales by total industry sales.
Market share provides a general idea of the size of a company in relation to its market and competitors.
Growing market share can be a sign of success, while falling market share may mean the opposite.
Ways to increase market share include implementing new technologies, generating customer loyalty, and acquiring competitors.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35106. Current, quick, and cash ratios are most commonly used to measure_____________.
questions.explain:
Liquidity refers to the ease with which an asset, or security, can be converted into ready cash without affecting its market price.
The two main types of liquidity are market liquidity and accounting liquidity.
Current, quick, and cash ratios are most commonly used to measure liquidity.

questions.question: 35105. An example of a __________________ was the English East India Company.
questions.explain:
Joint-stock companies are the ancestors of the modern-day corporation, although there are legal differences.
A joint-stock company is a business owned by its shareholders who can buy and sell shares freely.
Historically, the shareholders of a joint-stock company could bear unlimited liability for debts owed by the company.
In the U.S., incorporation limits shareholder liability to the face value of their shares.1
An example of a joint-stock company was the English East India Company.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35104. _______________ describes the flow of money and how people, companies, and governments make, save, invest, borrow, and spend it?
questions.explain:
Finance describes the flow of money and how people, companies, and governments make, save, invest, borrow, and spend it. Personal finance is about budgeting, spending, borrowing, saving, and investing for the future. Corporate finance involves raising capital and issuing stock. establishing and expanding a business, purchasing equipment, leasing machinery, and hiring staff. Public finance focuses on managing public debt, spending on public services, collecting taxes, and stimulating the economy. Finance is critical to growing wealth, making decisions, and managing risk.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35103. _________________ is an investment fund that holds multiple underlying assets and can be bought and sold on an exchange, much like an individual stock.
questions.explain:
An exchange-traded fund is a basket of securities that trades on an exchange just like a stock.
ETF share prices fluctuate throughout the trading day unlike mutual funds, which only trade once a day after the market closes.
ETFs offer low expense ratios and fewer brokerage commissions than buying stocks individually.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35102. Profit maximization ignores _____________.
questions.explain:
Profit Maximization:
Based on increase of sales or profits 
Emphasize on short term goals
Ignores time value of money
Ignores risk and uncertainty

questions.question: 35101. Sharholders wealth in a firm is represented by_________
questions.option1: the number of people employed in the firm
questions.option2: the book value of the firm’s assets less book value of the liabilities
questions.option3: the amount of salary paid to employee
questions.option4: the market price price per share of the firm’s common stock
questions.explain: Wealth = Price per share × Number of shares

questions.question: 35100. Which is not a characteristics of Financial Lease?
questions.option1: The PV of lease payments is less than 90% of the asset's fair market value.
questions.option2: Ownership transfers to the lessee at the end of the lease term
questions.option3: The terms equal or exceed 75% of the asset's estimated useful life
questions.option4: All risk is transferred to the lessee.
questions.explain:
Financial Lease:
Ownership: Ownership transfers to the lessee at the end of the lease term.

Bargain purchase options: These options enable the lessee to buy an asset at less than fair market value.

Terms: The terms equal or exceed 75% of the asset's estimated useful life.

Present value: PV of lease payments equals or exceeds 90% of the asset's original cost.

Risks/benefits: All risk is transferred to the lessee.

questions.question: 35099. Which of the following options is not a source of Short Term Finance?
questions.explain:

questions.question: 35098. _____________ focuses on internal financial operations, including accounting, financial reporting, and compliance.
questions.explain:
The Controller focuses on internal financial operations, including accounting, financial reporting, and compliance. 
 

The Treasurer, on the other hand, manages external financial activities, such as cash management, investments, and relationships with financial institutions.

questions.question: 35097. EPS = ?
questions.option4: Price per share × Number of shares
questions.explain:
Earnings per share (EPS) is a company's net income subtracted by preferred dividends and then divided by the number of common shares it has outstanding.
EPS indicates how much money a company makes for each share of its stock and is a widely used metric for estimating corporate value.
A higher EPS indicates greater value because investors will pay more for a company's shares if they think the company has higher profits relative to its share price.
EPS can be arrived at in several forms, such as excluding extraordinary items or discontinued operations, or on a diluted basis.
Like other financial metrics, earnings per share is most valuable when compared against competitor metrics, companies of the same industry, or across a period of time.

Source: Investopedia.

questions.question: 35096. Which is an investment strategy that involves spreading your investment capital across a variety of assets or securities within your investment portfolio?
questions.option1: Principle of Risk and Return(ঝুঁকি ও মুনাফা নীতি)
questions.option2: Principle of Profitability and Liquidity(তারল্য ও মুনাফা নীতি)
questions.option3: Principle of Portfolio Diversification(পোর্টফোলিও বৈচিত্র্যায়নের নীতি)
questions.option4: Principle of Time value of Money(অর্থের সময় মূল্যের নীতি)
questions.explain: Portfolio diversification is an investment strategy that involves spreading your investment capital across a variety of assets or securities within your investment portfolio. The aim of diversification is to reduce risk and increase the likelihood of achieving more stable and consistent returns over time.

questions.question: 35095. Which is the simplest form of business structure where a single individual owns and manages the entire business?
questions.explain:
The simplest form of business structure where a single individual owns and manages the entire business. 
 
There's no legal distinction between the owner and the business; they are considered one and the same entity. 

This means the owner is personally liable for all business debts and obligations

questions.question: 35094. In which business, personal assets are not separated from business assets?
questions.explain: Sole proprietorships and partnership do not produce a separate business entity. This means your business assets and liabilities are not separate from your personal assets and liabilities. You can be held personally liable for the debts and obligations of the business.

questions.question: 35093. _______________ is a hybrid form of capital that combines elements of debt and equity, often used by companies to fund growth, acquisitions, or other significant projects.
questions.explain:
• Mezzanine financing is a way for companies to raise funds for specific projects or to aid with an acquisition through a hybrid of debt and equity financing.
  • Mezzanine lending is also used in mezzanine funds, which are pooled investments, similar to mutual funds, that offer mezzanine financing to highly qualified businesses.
  • This type of financing can provide more generous returns to investors compared to typical corporate debt, often paying 12% to 30% a year.
  • Mezzanine loans are most commonly utilized in the expansion of established companies rather than as startup or early-phase financing.
  • Both mezzanine financing and preferred equity are subject to being called in and replaced by lower-interest financing if the market interest rate drops significantly.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35092. Budget is _________________________ .
questions.option1: a financial plan utilized by governments, businesses, and individuals of any income level.
questions.option2: a defined period that can greatly enhance the success of any financial undertaking.
questions.option3: Aside from earmarking resources, it can also aid in setting goals, measuring outcomes, and planning contingencies.
questions.explain:
A budget is a financial plan utilized by governments, businesses, and individuals of any income level.
A budget is usually for a defined period that can greatly enhance the success of any financial undertaking.
Corporate budgets are essential for operating at peak efficiency.
Aside from earmarking resources, a budget can also aid in setting goals, measuring outcomes, and planning contingencies.
Personal budgets are extremely useful in helping individuals and families manage their finances.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35091. ___________ is a fixed-income investment product where individuals lend money to a government or company at a specified interest rate for a predetermined period.
questions.explain:
A bond is a fixed-income instrument that pays a fixed interest rate or coupon to the holders.
Bond prices are inversely correlated with interest rates: when rates go up, bond prices fall, and vice versa.
Bonds are sold with maturity dates, which are the dates by which the principal amount must be paid back in full or risk default.

Source: Investopedia

questions.question: 35090. Which of the following is a source of Intermediate Term Financing?
questions.explain:
Intermediate-term financing
(1) term loans,

Long term financing
Internal: Promoter's initial capital, retained earnings, general reserve, dividend equalization fund, sinking fund, workers' compensation and welfare fund.
External: Common stock, preferred stock, bond or debenture, loans from bank or FIs.

questions.question: 35089. what is Capital Budgeting related to?
questions.option3: Long term as well as short term assets
questions.explain:
Capital budgeting relates to long terms resources. Capital planning is the cycle a business attempts to assess likely significant tasks or speculations.


Source: Unacademy

questions.question: 35088. _______________  is used by companies to evaluate major projects and investments, such as new plants or equipment.
questions.explain:
Capital budgeting is used by companies to evaluate major projects and investments, such as new plants or equipment. 
 

Capital Budgeting is the process involves analyzing a project's cash inflows and outflows to determine whether the expected return meets a set benchmark.

questions.explain:

questions.question: 35086. International Finance focuses on_________.
questions.explain: International Finance is the study of monetary interactions between two or more countries, focusing on areas such as foreign direct investment and currency exchange rates.

questions.explain:

questions.question: 35084. Who is called the father of 'Modern Finance'?
questions.explain:
Luca Pacioli, often referred to as the Father of Accounting, made significant contributions to the field of accounting, particularly through his introduction of the double-entry bookkeeping system.

Eugene Fama is often referred to as the "Father of Modern Finance" for his groundbreaking work on the efficient market hypothesis.

Peter Drucker is widely recognized as the "Father of Management". He is known for his extensive work in the field of business management, including his contributions to management theory and practice. 

The father of banking is often considered to be Alexander Hamilton, who played a crucial role in establishing the First Bank of the United States in 1791 and laid the foundation for the American banking system. He was instrumental in creating the nation's financial structure and served as the first Treasury Secretary.

questions.question: 35083. An unlimited liability company includes _________________  who are equally responsible for all debt and liabilities accrued by the business.
questions.explain:
An unlimited liability company includes general partnerships and sole proprietors who are equally responsible for all debt and liabilities accrued by the business.
Most companies opt to form limited partnerships in which a partner's liability can't exceed their investment in the company.
Nondisclosure is a benefit of forming a foreign unlimited liability subsidiary for many companies.

Source: Investopedia.

questions.question: 35082. Which of the following is considered as a limitation of Keynesian policies in developing countries?
questions.explain: যদিও কেইনসীয় অর্থনীতি চাহিদা বাড়িয়ে উৎপাদন বাড়ানোর পক্ষে, তবে উন্নয়নশীল দেশে অতিরিক্ত সরকারি ব্যয়ে ঘাটতি তৈরি হতে পারে। এই ঘাটতি ভবিষ্যতে মূল্যস্ফীতি, ঋণ বৃদ্ধি ও মুদ্রার মান হ্রাসের ঝুঁকি তৈরি করে। তাই এর প্রয়োগে ভারসাম্য প্রয়োজন। সীমাবদ্ধতা থাকা সত্ত্বেও তাৎক্ষণিক চাহিদা ও কর্মসংস্থান বৃদ্ধিতে এর যৌক্তিকতা স্পষ্ট।

questions.question: 35081. What does Keynesian economics recommend to address the lack of investment sensitivity in developing countries?
questions.option1: to decrease the rate of interest
questions.explain: উন্নয়নশীল দেশে বিনিয়োগকারীদের আস্থা কম থাকায় ব্যক্তিগত বিনিয়োগ যথেষ্ট হয় না। কেইনস বলেন, সরকারের উচিত নিজে অবকাঠামো, শিক্ষা, স্বাস্থ্য খাতে বিনিয়োগ করা। সরকারি বিনিয়োগ ‘multiplier’ প্রক্রিয়ায় চাহিদা বাড়ায়, ফলে বেসরকারি খাতও সক্রিয় হয়। এতে অর্থনৈতিক প্রবৃদ্ধি নিশ্চিত হয়, যা এই দেশের প্রেক্ষাপটে বাস্তব ও যৌক্তিক।

questions.question: 35080. What is the combined effect of a tax cut and an increase in government spending in Keynesian economics called?
questions.explain: কেইনসীয় দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিতে মন্দা বা বেকারত্ব দূর করতে কর হ্রাস এবং সরকারি ব্যয় বৃদ্ধি কার্যকর ভূমিকা রাখে। এ দুই নীতির সম্মিলনকে প্রসারণমূলক রাজস্বনীতি বলা হয়, যা চাহিদা বাড়িয়ে বিনিয়োগ ও কর্মসংস্থানের পরিবেশ তৈরি করে। উন্নয়নশীল দেশে সাধারণত ব্যক্তিগত খরচ ও বিনিয়োগ কম থাকে, ফলে রাষ্ট্রের এই হস্তক্ষেপ অর্থনীতিকে গতিশীল করে।

questions.question: 35079. Under which circumstances does Keynes advise the government to increase spending in the economies of developing countries?
questions.option4: if the value of money increases
questions.explain: উন্নয়নশীল দেশে উচ্চ বেকারত্ব ও উৎপাদন ঘাটতি সাধারণ সমস্যা। কেইনসীয় মতে, এই সমস্যা সমাধানে সরকার ব্যয় বাড়িয়ে বাজারে চাহিদা সৃষ্টির মাধ্যমে উৎপাদন বৃদ্ধি ও কর্মসংস্থান নিশ্চিত করতে পারে। চাহিদা বাড়লে বিনিয়োগ বাড়ে এবং অর্থনৈতিক চক্র সক্রিয় হয়। এইভাবে সরকার হস্তক্ষেপ করলে স্থবিরতা কাটে, যা উন্নয়নশীল অর্থনীতির জন্য উপযোগী।

questions.question: 35078. The concept of keeping the economy going by increasing demand through government expenditure in developing countries highlights which aspect of Keynesian economics?
questions.explain: কেইনসীয় অর্থনীতিতে কার্যকর চাহিদা একটি মূল ধারণা। উন্নয়নশীল দেশে বেকারত্ব ও উৎপাদন ঘাটতি দূর করতে সরকারের ব্যয় বাড়ানো হয় যাতে চাহিদা বাড়ে এবং বিনিয়োগ ও কর্মসংস্থান সৃষ্টি হয়। এই নীতিতে ধরা হয় যে, বাজার স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে পূর্ণ কর্মসংস্থান অর্জন করতে পারে না, বরং সরকারের হস্তক্ষেপ দরকার। তাই চাহিদা বাড়িয়ে উৎপাদন বাড়ানোর কৌশল কেইনসীয় যুক্তিকে দৃঢ় করে।

questions.question: 35077. If demand decreases, --
questions.explain: কেইনসীয় বিশ্লেষণে Aggregate Demand কমে গেলে উৎপাদন কমে, ফলে আয় ও কর্মসংস্থান কমে। এটি মন্দার কারণ হতে পারে।

questions.question: 35076. Which have the main role to determine income?
questions.explain: প্রাথমিক বিনিয়োগের মাধ্যমে অর্থনীতিতে গুণকের প্রক্রিয়া শুরু হয়। এটি সরাসরি আয় বৃদ্ধি করে এবং চাহিদা বাড়ায়।

questions.question: 35075. 'Only by increasing the Aggregate Demand economy can be circulated' it's the characteristics of --
questions.explain: কেইনস মনে করেন চাহিদাই অর্থনীতির চালিকাশক্তি। সরকার ব্যয় বাড়িয়ে Aggregate Demand বাড়ায় এবং স্থবির অর্থনীতি সচল করে।

questions.question: 35074. What do you mean by MPC + MPS ≠ 1 ?
questions.explain: MPC ও MPS দুটোই আয়ের অংশ। যদি তাদের যোগফল ১ না হয়, তবে তথ্য বা গণনায় ভুল হয়েছে। এটি একটি মৌলিক পরিচিতি।

questions.question: 35073. If MPS rises, multiplier will be--
questions.explain: যত বেশি আয় সঞ্চয় হয়, তত কম খরচ হয়। ফলে অর্থনীতিতে আয় পুনরাবৃত্তি কম হয় এবং গুণক কম হয়। গুণক = 1 / MPS।

questions.question: 35072. If MPC increases, income multiplier will --
questions.explain: MPC বাড়লে, অর্থনীতিতে বেশি ভোগ হয়। ফলে প্রাথমিক ব্যয়ের প্রভাব অনেক বেশি হয়ে পড়ে। তাই গুণক বাড়ে এবং আয়ের সামগ্রিক বৃদ্ধি বেশি হয়।

questions.question: 35071. What does it mean by 'a' in C = a + bY ?
questions.explain: ‘a’ হলো সেই ভোগ যা মানুষ আয়ের অস্তিত্ব না থাকলেও করে। এটি প্রয়োজনীয় ভোগ যা জীবনের জন্য অপরিহার্য, যেমন খাদ্য, বাসস্থান ইত্যাদি।

questions.question: 35070. When MPC = 0.8, Multiplier will be--
questions.explain: Multiplier = 1 / (1 - MPC) = 1 / (1 - 0.8) = 1 / 0.2 = 5। এর মানে হল, একটি বিনিয়োগ যদি ১০০ টাকা হয়, তবে তা মোট আয় ৫০০ টাকা পর্যন্ত বাড়াতে পারে।

questions.question: 35069. What is called Multiplier?
questions.explain: Multiplier বোঝায় প্রাথমিক বিনিয়োগ বা ব্যয়ের ফলে মোট জাতীয় আয়ের যতগুণ বৃদ্ধি ঘটে। এটি MPC-এর ভিত্তিতে নির্ধারিত হয় এবং অর্থনীতিতে বিনিয়োগ বা সরকারের ব্যয় কতটা প্রভাব ফেলবে তা বোঝাতে ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.question: 35068. MPC + MPS = ?
questions.explain: প্রাপ্ত আয় হয় ভোগ করা হয়, নয়তো সঞ্চয় করা হয়। তাই MPC (প্রান্তিক ভোগ প্রবণতা) ও MPS (প্রান্তিক সঞ্চয় প্রবণতা) এর যোগফল সর্বদা ১ হবে। এটি কেইনসীয় মডেলের একটি মৌলিক পরিচিতি।

questions.question: 35067. In Keynesian model, which is the main determinant to determine the income?
questions.explain:
কেইনসের মতে স্বল্পমেয়াদে উৎপাদন ও আয় নির্ধারিত হয় চাহিদার দ্বারা। সরবরাহ স্থিতিশীল ধরা হয়। তাই Aggregate Demand বাড়লে আয় বাড়ে। কমলে আয় হ্রাস পায়। এটি উৎপাদনের উপর সরাসরি প্রভাব ফেলে।
​
Keynesian মডেলে জাতীয় আয় (Aggregate Income) নির্ধারণ হয় মূলত Aggregate Demand বা মোট চাহিদার উপর ভিত্তি করে। Aggregate Demand নির্ধারণ করে উৎপাদনের মাত্রা, আর উৎপাদন মাত্রা নির্ধারণ করে আয়ের পরিমাণ। তাই এখানে প্রধান নিয়ামক হলো Aggregate Income.

questions.question: 35066. When MPC will be greater then multiplier will be--
questions.explain: আয় গুণকের সূত্র হলো 1/(1−MPC)। যদি MPC বেশি হয়, তাহলে 1−MPC ছোট হবে, ফলে গুণকের মান বড় হবে। অর্থাৎ, আয় যত বেশি, খরচ হয় তত বেশি। তা পরবর্তী ব্যক্তির আয়ের অংশ হয়ে অর্থনীতিতে বারবার গুণিত হয়ে ঘুরতে থাকে।

questions.question: 35065. According to Keynes, which doesn't change automatically?
questions.explain: কেইনসের মতে বিনিয়োগ নির্ভর করে উদ্যোক্তাদের প্রত্যাশা ও সুদের হারের ওপর, যা পরিবর্তনশীল হলেও স্বয়ংক্রিয় নয়। আয় পরিবর্তনের ফলে ভোগ ও সঞ্চয় পরিবর্তিত হলেও বিনিয়োগ এমন নয়। এটি নীতিনির্ধারক ও উদ্যোক্তার আস্থা এবং ভবিষ্যত লাভ প্রত্যাশার ভিত্তিতে নির্ধারিত হয়।

questions.question: 35064. Through which condition, equilibrium income will be determined in Keynesian income determination model?
questions.explain: কেইনসীয় আয় নির্ধারণ মডেল অনুযায়ী, ভারসাম্য আয় সেই বিন্দুতে অর্জিত হয় যেখানে পরিকল্পিত সঞ্চয় পরিকল্পিত বিনিয়োগের সমান হয়। যদি সঞ্চয় বেশি হয়, তবে চাহিদা কমে গিয়ে আয় কমবে; আবার সঞ্চয় কম হলে বিনিয়োগ বেশি হয়ে চাহিদা বাড়বে। তাই ভারস্যমূলক অবস্থায় সঞ্চয় ও বিনিয়োগ সমান হতে হবে।

questions.question: 35063. Who determines the monetary policy?
questions.explain: কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক হচ্ছে এমন একটি প্রতিষ্ঠান যা মুদ্রার সরবরাহ ও সুদের হার নিয়ন্ত্রণ করার মাধ্যমে দেশের সমগ্র অর্থব্যবস্থাকে পরিচালনা করে। এছাড়াও কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক বিনিময় হার নিয়ন্ত্রণ, বাণিজ্য সম্পরসারণ, মুদ্রা-মান সংরক্ষণ ও সরকারের ব্যাংক হিসেবে কাজ করে। সরকারের পক্ষে মুদ্রানীতি প্রণয়ন করে তা বাস্তবায়নে সার্বিক সহায়তা, পরামর্শ ও কার্যক্রম পরিচালনায় অন্যান্য ব্যাংকেরও ব্যাংক হিসেবে দায়িত্ব পালন করে কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যাংক।
